notes: Job POSTTRAN step STEP15: CardDemo's own daily transactions posted against its accounts, cross references and category balances. Every input is the corpus's data. Derived from CardDemo (Apache-2.0; Copyright Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates): LICENSE and NOTICE here are the source's own. #4049 (the test-strengthening loop, tests/tools/strengthen.py, claude-sonnet-5-5; the expected results are the COBOL's own): records appended to DALYTRAN (dailytran.txt) -- expired-one-day-before-orig: Account 2 expires 2024-08-11, so this is the first record to take the 103 expired branch; the shifted-offset comparison would not reject it.; orig-date-equals-expiry: The date equals the account expiry date, so the original posts the record while a comparison that also rejects equal dates would reject it.; orig-year-1999-shifted-offset: The shifted slice starts with '9', which is greater than the expiry's leading '2', so the mutant wrongly rejects this valid record and the original posts it.; orig-ts-far-after-expiry-valid-card: A valid card and a tiny amount reach the expiry comparison, with an origination date far past any account expiry so the false branch (reason 103) is taken.; expiry-fail-second-account-small-amt: A second account with a minimal amount and a far-future origination date reaches the expired-account rejection without tripping the overlimit check..

faults.name: card-not-found

faults.name: xref-read-error-posts-stale
faults.why: 30 on the second cross-reference READ (IBM Enterprise COBOL for z/OS Language Reference, File status key values): no INVALID KEY and no status test, so the program posts the second transaction against the FIRST one's account (the program's defect) -- the step goes on

faults.name: account-read-error-posts-stale
